Eighth Moon [224 Sep 1 – Sep 30], made a navy, personally rode dragon boat, followed the Cài and Yǐng, sailed the Huái, visited Shòuchūn.  Yáng Province’s border officers and clerks and servicemen and civilians that had violations of five years punishment on down were all pardoned and released. 
Ninth Moon [224 Oct 1 – Oct 29], therefore reached Guǎnglíng, amnesty on Qīng and Xú two provinces, changed and replaced the various officers and administrators.
Winter, Tenth Moon [224 Oct 30 – Nov 28], Yǐmǎo [224 Nov 4], Tàibái during daytime seen. Traveled back to Xǔchāng Palace. <a href="#annotation-41" id="source-41">[41]</a>
Eleventh Moon [224 Nov 29 – Dec 27], Gēngyín [224 Dec 9], because Jì Province was in famine, sent envoys to open the granaries to relieve them. Wùshēn [224 Dec 27], last day of the moon, the sun was eclipsed.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
五年春正月，初令謀反大逆乃得相告，其餘皆勿聽治；敢妄相告，以其罪罪之。三月，行自許昌還洛陽宮。夏四月，立太學，制五經課試之法，置春秋穀梁博士。五月，有司以公卿朝朔望日，因奏疑事，聽斷大政，論辨得失。秋七月，行東巡，幸許昌宮。八月，為水軍，親御龍舟，循蔡、潁，浮淮，幸壽春。揚州界將吏士民，犯五歲刑已下，皆原除之。九月，遂至廣陵，赦青、徐二州，改易諸將守。冬十月乙卯，太白晝見。行還許昌宮。〔一〕十一月庚寅，以冀州饑，遣使者開倉廩振之。戊申晦，日有食之。
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-41" id="annotation-41">[41]</a> Wèi shū records the Guǐyǒu [224 Nov 22] Edict stating: “If the near are not soothed, how can the far be embraced? Now tasks are many but the people are few, above and below use written law to damage one another, the Hundred Surnames have no way to use their hands and feet. In the past the weeper at Tàishān believed that an oppressive government was more ferocious than tigers.  I am equipped with the airs of the classicists, submit to the remnant teachings of the sages, how can I amuse my eyes with their words but yet in conduct violate their prohibitions? Widely discuss lightening punishments, to give kindness to the Hundred Surnames.”
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏書載癸酉詔曰：「近之不綏，何遠之懷？今事多而民少，上下相弊以文法，百姓無所措其手足。昔太山之哭者，以為苛政甚于猛虎，吾備儒者之風，服聖人之遺教，豈可以目翫其辭，行違其誡者哉？廣議輕刑，以惠百姓。」
:::
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Twelfth Moon [224 Dec 28 – 225 Jan 26], Edict said: “The Former Kings regulated Ritual, in order to manifest filial piety and serve the ancestors, the largest then were the Suburb and Altars, the next the Ancestral Temples, the Three Celestials and Five Transitions, the famed mountains and great rivers.  Those not of this kind are not in the sacrificial canon. In the final eras of decline and chaos, there is veneration and faith in witchcraft and seers, reaching into the Palace Halls and among the doors and windows, none are not flooded in libations, so extreme is the confusion. From now on, those that dare set offerings for improper sacrifices or speak of witchcraft prayers, all are to be arrested for deviant ways and theories. Make this known in orders and law.” That year dug Tiānyuān pond.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
十二月，詔曰：「先王制禮，所以昭孝事祖，大則郊社，其次宗廟，三辰五行，名山大川，非此族也，不在祀典。叔世衰亂，崇信巫史，至乃宮殿之內，戶牖之閒，無不沃酹，甚矣其惑也。自今，其敢設非祀之祭，巫祝之言，皆以執左道論，著于令典。」是歲穿天淵池。
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Sixth Year, Spring, Second Moon [225 Feb 25 – Mar 26], sent envoys to travel from Xǔchāng on east thoroughly to Pèi prefecture, to inquire the people of their pains and sufferings, and give support and loans to the poor. <a href="#annotation-42" id="source-42">[42]</a> Third Moon [225 Mar 27 – Apr 25], traveled to visit Shàolíng, connected Tǎolǔ Canal.  Yǐsì [Apr 23], returned to Xǔchāng Palace. Bìng Province Inspector Liáng Xí suppressed the Xiānbēi [chieftain] Kē Bĭnéng, greatly defeated him.  Xīnwèi,  the Emperor made navy on eastern campaign.
Fifth Moon [225 Jun 24 – Jul 22], Wùshēn [225 Jun 25], visited Qiáo. Rénxū [225 Jul 9], Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
六年春二月，遣使者循行許昌以東盡沛郡，問民所疾苦，貧者振貸之。〔一〕三月，行幸召陵，通討虜渠。乙巳，還許昌宮。并州刺史梁習討鮮卑軻比能，大破之。辛未，帝為舟師東征。五月戊申，幸譙。壬戌，熒惑入太微。
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-42" id="annotation-42">[42]</a> Wèi lüè records the Edict stating: “In the past Xuānyuán established titles on four sides, Zhōu Wǔ said: ‘I have governing officials of ten men.’  These probably were how the former sages systemized the state and ruled the people, brightened and achieved Heaven’s labors, treated having many worthies as nobility. Now the interior has the Excellencies and Ministers to defend the capital, the exterior establishes Governors and Earls to supervise the Four Quarters. As for the primary army going out on campaign, then the army’s center should also have the stone pillar of a worthy commander, and where the heavy supplies are located also should have an important minister to defend and maintain, and only then afterward the Chariot Carriage can travel around Heaven’s Under without worrying of the interior or exterior. I now will campaign against rebels, and wish to maintain this for accumulated years. Thus appoint the Secretariat Writers Director and Marquess of Yǐng village Chén Qún as Defending Army General-in-Chief and the Secretariat Writers Deputy-Director and Marquess of Xī village Sīmǎ Yì as Succoring Army General-in-Chief.  If I overlook the Jiāng to confer on the various officers policies and strategies, then the Succoring Army will remain at Xǔchāng to command the rear’s various armies and manage the rear Terrace’s written document affairs, and the Defending Army will accompany the Chariot Carriage to direct and command the multitudes and armies and manage the traveling Secretariat Writers affairs. Both are Lent Staves and drums and horns, given Central Army soldiers and cavalry of six hundred men. I wish to build Palace Residences several lǐ from the Jiāng, go back and forth from it, and on seeing an appearance of when the rebels can be struck, to then send out surprise troops to strike them, and if perhaps they cannot [be struck], then I will deploy the Six Armies with hunting expeditions, feast and bestow on the army servicemen.”
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏略載詔曰：「昔軒轅建四面之號，周武稱『予有亂臣十人』，斯蓋先聖所以體國君民，亮成天工，多賢為貴也。今內有公卿以鎮京師，外設牧伯以監四方，至於元戎出征，則軍中宜有柱石之賢帥，輜重所在，又宜有鎮守之重臣，然後車駕可以周行天下，無內外之慮。吾今當征賊，欲守之積年。其以尚書令潁鄉侯陳群為鎮軍大將軍，尚書僕射西鄉侯司馬懿為撫軍大將軍。若吾臨江授諸將方略，則撫軍當留許昌，督後諸軍，錄後臺文書事；鎮軍隨車駕，當董督眾軍，錄行尚書事；皆假節鼓吹，給中軍兵騎六百人。吾欲去江數里，築宮室，往來其中，見賊可擊之形，便出奇兵擊之；若或未可，則當舒六軍以遊獵，饗賜軍士。」
:::
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Sixth Moon [225 Jul 23 – Aug 21], Lìchéng prefecture soldier Cài Fāng and others with the prefecture rebelled, killing Administrator Xú Zhì.  Sent Garrison Cavalry Colonel Rén Fú and Infantry Colonel Duàn Zhāo with the Qīng Province Inspector to suppress and pacified them.  Those that had met with coercion and those that had deserted were all pardoned for their crimes.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
六月，利成郡兵蔡方等以郡反，殺太守徐質。遣屯騎校尉任福、步兵校尉段昭與青州刺史討平之；其見脅略及亡命者，皆赦其罪。
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Autumn, Seventh Moon [225 Aug 22 – Sep 19], enthroned the Imperial son [Cáo] Jiàn as King of Dōngwǔyáng. 
Eighth Moon [225 Sep 20 – Oct 19], the Emperor therefore with the navy from Qiáo followed the Guō to enter the Huái, followed land roads to visit Xú [Province]. Ninth Moon [225 Oct 20 – Nov 17], built Dōngxún Terrace. 
Winter, Tenth Moon [225 Nov 18 – Dec 17] traveled to visit Guǎnglíng former city, overlooked the Jiāng to observe the soldiers, the military troops over a hundred thousand, banners and flags across several hundred lǐ. <a href="#annotation-43" id="source-43">[43]</a> That year, great cold, the waterways froze, the boats could not enter the Jiāng, thus drew back and returned.
Eleventh Moon [225 Dec 18 – 226 Jan 15], the King of Dōngwǔyáng [Cáo] Jiàn died.
Twelfth Moon [226 Jan 16 – Feb 14], traveled from Qiáo, passed Liáng, sent envoy with Grand Offering to sacrifice to former Hàn’s Grand Commandant Qiáo Xuán.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
秋七月，立皇子鑒為東武陽王。八月，帝遂以舟師自譙循渦入淮，從陸道幸徐。九月，築東巡臺。冬十月，行幸廣陵故城，臨江觀兵，戎卒十餘萬，旌旗數百里。〔一〕是歲大寒，水道冰，舟不得入江，乃引還。十一月，東武陽王鑒薨。十二月，行自譙過梁，遣使以太牢祀故漢太尉橋玄。
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-43" id="annotation-43">[43]</a> Wèi shū records the Emperor’s on horseback composed poem stating:
> Observing troops overlooking the Jiāng’s waters
> The water’s flow how it rushes and rushes!
> Spears and pikes create a mountain forest
> Dark armor gleams in the sun’s light
> Fierce officers harbor violent rage
> Courageous spirit right about to be unleashed
> Who says the Jiāng’s waters are wide?
> One reed could be a boat 
> Without battle subduing enemy caitiffs
> Restraining weapons is praised as worthy and good
> Gǔ-gōng residing at Qíyì
> Truly was the beginning of cutting down Yīn-Shāng 
> Mèng Xiàn camped at Hǔláo
> The Zhèng man were afraid and bowed head 
> Chōngguó attended to plowing and planting
> The Xiānlíng on their own were broken and destroyed 
> Raising farms between the Huái and Sì
> Building house and capital in Xú region 
> Measuring appropriate fortune and expedient strategy
> The Six Armies all pleased and quiet
> How can it be like Dōngshān’s ode?
> Many, many, its numerous sorrows and wounds.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏書載帝於馬上為詩曰：「觀兵臨江水，水流何湯湯！戈矛成山林，玄甲耀日光。猛將懷暴怒，膽氣正從橫。誰云江水廣，一葦可以航，不戰屈敵虜，戢兵稱賢良。古公宅岐邑，實始翦殷商。孟獻營虎牢，鄭人懼稽顙。充國務耕植，先零自破亡。興農淮、泗間，築室都徐方。量宜運權略，六軍咸悅康；豈如東山詩，悠悠多憂傷。」
:::
:::
:::

## Huángchū 7 (226) {.unnumbered}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Seventh Year, Spring, Standard Moon [226 Feb 15 – Mar 15], about to visit Xǔchāng, Xǔchāng city’s south gate without reason on its own collapsed. The Emperor in his heart hated this, and therefore did not enter.  Rénzǐ [226 Feb 24], traveled back to Luòyáng Palace.
Third Moon [226 Apr 15 – May 13], built Jiǔhuá Terrace. 
Summer, Fifth Moon [226 Jun 13 – Jul 11], Bǐngchén [226 Jun 28], the Emperor was critically ill, summoned Central Army General-in-Chief Cáo Zhēn, Defending Army General-in-Chief Chén Qún, Campaigning East General-in-Chief Cáo Xiū, Succoring Army General-in-Chief Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng, to together receive Legacy Edict to assist the successor ruler.  Dismissed the Rear Palace’s Shūyuán and Zhāoyí on down to return to their families.  Dīngsì [226 Jun 29], the Emperor passed away in Jiāfú Hall, at the time his years forty.  <a href="#annotation-44" id="source-44">[44]</a>
Sixth Moon [226 Jul 12 – Aug 10], Wùyín [226 Jul 20], buried at Shǒuyánglíng. From the encoffining to the burial, all followed the specifications in his Final Regulations. <a href="#annotation-45" id="source-45">[45]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
七年春正月，將幸許昌，許昌城南門無故自崩，帝心惡之，遂不入。壬子，行還洛陽宮。三月，築九華臺。夏五月丙辰，帝疾篤，召中軍大將軍曹真、鎮軍大將軍陳群、征東大將軍曹休、撫軍大將軍司馬宣王，並受遺詔輔嗣主。遣後宮淑媛、昭儀已下歸其家。丁巳，帝崩于嘉福殿，時年四十。〔一〕六月戊寅，葬首陽陵。自殯及葬，皆以終制從事。〔二〕
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-44" id="annotation-44">[44]</a> Wèi shū states: Encoffined in Chónghuá Front Hall.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏書曰：殯於崇華前殿。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-45" id="annotation-45">[45]</a> Wèishì Chūnqiū states: Emperor Míng  was about to escort the burial, Cáo Zhēn, Chén Qún, Wáng Lǎng and others due to the [dangerous] summer heat firmly remonstrated, so he stopped.

Sūn Shèng states: The task of burying the grave is the filial son’s utmost pain. Of the ways of human affairs, in this none are heavier. Therefore, ‘Heaven’s Son in the Seventh Moon is buried, those of the same course completely arrive.’  Even for the emotions of righteous feeling, yet one would be thorough in the grieving at facing the burial tunnel, so all the more for natural feelings coming from within, the respect of Ritual would value it! The virtue of the Wèi dynasty was not a foundation for many generations. In the past Huà Yuán lavishly buried and noble men believed it abandoning his lord to evil.  The remonstrations of [Chén] Qún and the rest, the abandonment was how much more extreme!

The Marquess of Juànchéng [Cáo] Zhí  made an elegy that said:

“On Huángchū Seventh Year Fifth Moon Seventeenth Day,  the Greatly Departed Imperial Emperor Passed Away.  Alas the Sorrow! At the time Heaven thundered and Earth quaked, collapsing mountains and falling frost, the sun’s essence dimmed in light, the Five Latitudes traveled wrong,  the Hundred Surnames cried aloud, Myriad States sorrowful and pained, like mourning for deceased father and deceased mother, melancholy and longing surpassing Táng [Yáo],  beating chest and stomping in the suburbs and wilderness, looking up to ponder the vast blue [sky], all saying: ‘What crime [was there], to early perish and fall? Alas the Sorrow!’ Grieving for the Greatly Departed, suddenly how light is extinguished, forever abandoning the Myriad States, clouds departing and rain dried away. Continuing to ask into the desolation, confused and dumb choking with sobs, from the sleeve drawing the blade, sighing to seek my own death, to chase after the Three Good Men,  willing in heart to share a grave, in emotion pondering the South Wind,  thoughts melancholy and slow, to in the end accompany in destruction, pointing to the sun as oath. Investigating the various former records, searching for wise words: life is like a floating passing, only virtue can be discussed; in morning heard and at evening dying, what Kǒng’s records preserved.  Though the Imperial is gone, Heaven’s blessings forever extend. How to narrate virtue? Memorialize it on white silks. How to sing of achievements? Declare it in pipes and strings. Thus I made an elegy saying:

‘Bright bright the Grand Essence, the Two Polarities first separated, the center harmonizing to create matter, originating human order,  thus reaching the Three Augusts, they filled and maintained the true way, passing down to the Five Emperors, they continued it with exemplary purity,  the Three Dynasties made systems, followed the footsteps to establish achievement.  The last successors did not maintain, the [social] fabric slackened to Qín, collapsing music and extinguishing scholarship, classicists buried and ritual [books] burned, two generations and then destroyed.  The Hàn clan then followed, not seeking the ancient teachings, Yíng Zhèng was imitated,  the King’s networks and Emperor’s canons thus were quieted and not heard. The fading light was secluded and dark, the Way exhausted and fortunes shifted, Qián and Kūn cycled in calendar, selected the sagely and appointed the worthy, thus embracing the Greatly Departed, to entrust him with the numerous individuals.  A dragon flying to initiate the blessings, in accord with the highest mysteries, the Five Transitions settled in order, he changed the title and revised the year,  brilliant brilliant radiant radiant, he received the Mandate from Heaven. His benevolent air descended on all, virtue by ritual spread, his auspicious nature and sagely character, towering in youthful beauty. He mastered the Six Canons,  learned without leaving the courtyard,  devoted heart without fail, raising his will to the azure sky. Talent and refinement elegant and bright, like the luster of jade, he heard and discerned the soundless, gazed and saw the invisible. His firmness was like metal, his integrity like jasper, like the purity of ice, like the evenness of whetstones. He granted noble titles without bias, punished criminals without lenience, his heart reflected on all affairs, illuminated the feelings of those below. Wishing for good arms and legs [assistant ministers], praising the past’s Yī [Yǐn] and Lǚ [Shàng], he searched and raised up the low, citing [Shāng] Tāng and imitating [Xià] Yǔ, he drew out talents from mountain caves, chose servicemen from disheveled doors, only virtue was considered, no constraints by ancestry. On the surface of the settled land, morality and righteousness was his planning, not blocking away by rugged terrain, the Six Directions were his concern. Fair covenant was universally honored, below to purify the people, he expanded and developed standards and regulations, continuing on from predecessors. Law codes and rank systems, praised or censured by cause. He rode the chariots of Yīn, enacted the seasons of Xià.  Gold Root Yellow Canopy,  kingfisher feathers and dragon scales, robes and crown esteemed and beautiful, hanging tassels renewed, venerable and solemn in ritual expression, he appeared like a divinity. Regional governors wonderfully raised, reverent in sympathizing with the people, tiger officers carried insignia, defending the four borders. Wherever the vermilion flags cut down, the Nine Soils were shaken,  who dared not comply, who dared not be a servant? Hanging banners by the sea, across ten thousand lǐ there was no dust. The caitiff [Liú] Bèi viciously pierced, birds falling at the Jiāng and Mín, [Sūn] Quán like a beached fish, dried and shriveled scales,  the Sùshèn paid tribute, the Yuècháng delivered treasures, the Tiáozhī in cutoff regions sent sons as attendants to inwardly submit.  Virtue comparable to the Former Imperials, achievements comparable to grand antiquity. The spirits above sent down signs, the Yellow Beginning [Huángchū] received the blessings, the Hé’s dragon and Luò’s turtle,  crossed waves to roam downstream, level and balanced as measuring ropes, divine birds soared and danced, numerous jiá in the steps sprouted,  restrained winds fanned away summer heat, white beasts and white birds, flew and ran in the suburbs and wilds, divine bells and treasure cauldrons, forms emerging from old earth,  clouds blossoming sweet dew, rained and applied on the roofs, Língzhī grew in ponds, Zhūhuá shaded the shores.  Swirling swirling the gentle wind, vast vast the sweet rain, sowed and reaped in abundance, our grain and our millet. Families girdled in the kindness of the lord, households immersed in the compassion of the father. He planned to deliver Grand Harmony,  according with virtue and preserving righteousness, right about to ascend Jièshān, with the Former Imperial forming a pair,  engraving stone to chronicle the merits, simultaneously recording the multitudes of omens, expanding the Fēng-Shàn [sacrifices],  assigning the achievement to Heaven and Earth, host rituals for the hundred spirits, the standards of merit and fate observed, the Viewing Sacrifices to the Four Peaks,  burning and conferring offered firewood, solemn in the South Suburbs, ancestral sacrifices to the Highest God, three sacrificial animals all provided,  summer Dì autumn Cháng [sacrifices],  inaugural lords accompanied in sacrifices, proffering jade rings and presenting jade tablets. Phoenix carriage shadowy and vast,  dragon flag grand ceremonies, thus reaching Tài Temple, bells and drums sounded and sounded, eulogizing virtue and singing of achievement, eight rows of dancers swaying and swaying.  The Imperial Ancestors thus fed, the illustrious father [Cáo Cāo] came to feast, the spirit satisfied and liquor finished, sending down good fortune. Heaven and Earth quaked and shook, so the Greatly Departed calmed them. The three celestials were dark and hidden, so the Greatly Departed illuminated them. The Imperial bonds were cut off, so the Greatly Departed weaved them. The Divine Vessels were not gathered, so the Greatly Departed managed them. Ritual and Music were neglected, so the Greatly Departed spread them. Benevolence and Righteousness were submerged, so the Greatly Departed raised them. Hidden Dragon Concealed Phoenix, so the Greatly Departed flew them. The distant Dí abandoned prosperity,  so the Greatly Departed rectified them. On the Throne seven years, the foundational achievement was yet raised, about to have eternal Grand Harmony, surpassing the legacies of the Three [Augusts] and Five [Emperors], he should have been a teacher for all, expanding as a divine ruler, lifespan outlasting metal and stone, equaling the count of Dōngfù,  how could he suddenly be lost, sending body to Lordly Earth, leaving us desolate desolate, without one to gaze to and without one to rely on. Oh august heavens, how can you be so cruel? Alas the Sorrow! Clearly investigating good or bad fortune, understanding from afar survival or destruction, he deeply passed down canon regulations, extending to the successor Imperial [Cáo Ruì]. The sagely ascended [Cáo Ruì] reverently serves [Cáo Pī’s Final Regulations], to follow and to enact, thus creates the Dark Rooms, foundation at Shǒuyáng,  following the path of Gǔlín, recalling Yáo of admirable Táng,  with the mountain sharing tomb, no trees no boundaries, pottery carriages and straw effigies, pearls and jade not stored.  A hundred divinities alert in attention, coming guests in the secluded hall, farm birds field beasts, watch for the flight of the soul. Therefore, waiting for the great Passage’s completion, xī, selecting the auspicious time’s good fortune.  Concealing flowery body in the catalpa coffin, xī, resting in the Main Hall to house the spirit.  Looking back to the see the successor’s wails, xī, observing the attendees’ sorrowful sounds.  Mourning that the Delayed Carriage is already prepared, xī, emotional at the Appearance Chariot’s fast journey.  Floating the flying soul to the light clouds, xī, to the yellow ruins to extinguish the [bodily] form.  Turning back on the Three Lights shining clear, xī, returning to the Dark Room’s gloomy depths.  Oh once gone there is no return, xī, pained by the closed doors forever locked. Oh Your Distant Servant’s solitary distance, xī, moved by the horrific unspeakable to grief and shock.  Heart isolated and cutoff with nowhere to express [my sorrow], xī, numerous flowing tears crossing the neck.  Pondering your grace and glory to rashly run [to you], xī, obstructed by the gate passes’ lofty towers. Looking back to my mourning sash to recklessly set out, xī, constrained by the passes binding me.  Wishing to fly high and distantly rest [at your tomb], xī, fearing the far spread of Heaven’s Net.  Distantly throwing my bones to the foot of your mountain, xī, to repay your kindness and nurture in the Lower Court.  Indignantly beating chest and self-lamenting, xī, fearing that your bestowals were heavy and my life is light. Sighing, the trifling drive to action, xī, sweetly willing for nine deaths and forgetting life. Almost in the director of life’s conscription registers,  xī, before the yellow haired  to fall and wither. Heaven covers high but examines the low, xī, I hope that the divine intelligence listens to us. Alone and desolate but with none to tell, xī, I look back to my shadow and pity the form. Presenting this document to write thoughts, xī, I join brush and ink to lay out my sincerity. Alas the Sorrow!’”

〔二〕　魏氏春秋曰：明帝將送葬，曹真、陳群、王朗等以暑熱固諫，乃止。孫盛曰：夫窀穸之事，孝子之極痛也，人倫之道，於斯莫重。故天子七月而葬，同軌畢至。夫以義感之情，猶盡臨隧之哀，況乎天性發中，敦禮者重之哉！魏氏之德，仍世不基矣。昔華元厚葬，君子以為棄君於惡，群等之諫，棄孰甚焉！鄄城侯植為誄曰：「惟黃初七年五月七日，大行皇帝崩，嗚呼哀哉！于時天震地駭，崩山隕霜，陽精薄景，五緯錯行，百姓呼嗟，萬國悲傷，若喪考妣，（恩過慕）〔思慕過〕唐，擗踊郊野，仰想穹蒼，僉曰何辜，早世殞喪，嗚呼哀哉！悲夫大行，忽焉光滅，永棄萬國，雲往雨絕。承問荒忽，惛懵哽咽，袖鋒抽刃，歎自僵斃，追慕三良，甘心同穴。感惟南風，惟以鬱滯，終於偕沒，指景自誓。考諸先記，尋之哲言，生若浮寄，唯德可論，朝聞夕逝，孔志所存。皇雖一沒，天祿永延，何以述德？表之素旃。何以詠功？宣之管絃。乃作誄曰：皓皓太素，兩儀始分，中和產物，肇有人倫，爰暨三皇，實秉道真，降逮五帝，繼以懿純，三代制作，踵武立勳。季嗣不維，網漏于秦，崩樂滅學，儒坑禮焚，二世而殲，漢氏乃因，弗求古訓，嬴政是遵，王綱帝典，闃爾無聞。末光幽昧，道究運遷，乾坤迴曆，簡聖授賢，乃眷大行，屬以黎元。龍飛啟祚，合契上玄，五行定紀，改號革年，明明赫赫，受命于天。仁風偃物，德以禮宣；祥惟聖質，嶷在幼妍。庶幾六典，學不過庭，潛心無罔，抗志青冥。才秀藻朗，如玉之瑩，聽察無嚮，瞻睹未形。其剛如金，其貞如瓊，如冰之潔，如砥之平。爵公無私，戮違無輕，心鏡萬機，攬照下情。思良股肱，嘉昔伊、呂，搜揚側陋，舉湯代禹；拔才巖穴，取士蓬戶，唯德是縈，弗拘禰祖。宅土之表，道義是圖，弗營厥險，六合是虞。齊契共遵，下以純民，恢拓規矩，克紹前人。科條品制，褒貶以因。乘殷之輅，行夏之辰。金根黃屋，翠葆龍鱗，紼冕崇麗，衡紞維新，尊肅禮容，矚之若神。方牧妙舉，欽於恤民，虎將荷節，鎮彼四鄰；朱旗所剿，九壤被震，疇克不若？孰敢不臣？縣旌海表，萬里無塵。虜備凶徹，鳥殪江岷，權若涸魚，乾腊矯鱗，肅慎納貢，越裳效珍，條支絕域，侍子內賓。德儕先皇，功侔太古。上靈降瑞，黃初叔祜：河龍洛龜，淩波游下；平鈞應繩，神鸞翔舞；數莢階除，系風扇暑；皓獸素禽，飛走郊野；神鍾寶鼎，形自舊土；雲英甘露，瀸塗被宇；靈芝冒沼，朱華蔭渚。回回凱風，祁祁甘雨，稼穡豐登，我稷我黍。家佩惠君，戶蒙慈父。圖致太和，洽德全義。將登介山，先皇作儷。鐫石紀勳，兼錄眾瑞，方隆封禪，歸功天地，賓禮百靈，勳命視規，望祭四嶽，燎封奉柴，肅于南郊，宗祀上帝。三牲既供，夏禘秋嘗，元侯佐祭，獻璧奉璋。鸞輿幽藹，龍旂太常，爰迄太廟，鍾鼓鍠鍠，頌德詠功，八佾鏘鏘。皇祖既饗，烈考來享，神具醉止，降茲福祥。天地震蕩，大行康之；三辰暗昧，大行光之；皇紘絕維，大行綱之；神器莫統，大行當之；禮樂廢弛，大行張之；仁義陸沈，大行揚之；潛龍隱鳳，大行翔之；疏狄遐康，大行匡之。在位七載，元功仍舉，將永太和，絕跡三五，宜作物師，長為神主，壽終金石，等算東父，如何奄忽，摧身后土，俾我〈煢，去冖〉〈煢，去冖〉，靡瞻靡顧。嗟嗟皇穹，胡寧忍務？嗚呼哀哉！明監吉凶，體遠存亡，深垂典制，申之嗣皇。聖上虔奉，是順是將，乃創玄宇，基為首陽，擬跡穀林，追堯慕唐，合山同陵，不樹不疆，塗車芻靈，珠玉靡藏。百神警侍，來賓幽堂，耕禽田獸，望魂之翔。於是，俟大隧之致功兮，練元辰之淑禎，潛華體於梓宮兮，馮正殿以居靈。顧望嗣之號咷兮，存臨者之悲聲，悼晏駕之既脩兮，感容車之速征。浮飛魂於輕霄兮，就黃墟以滅形，背三光之昭晰兮，歸玄宅之冥冥。嗟一往之不反兮，痛閟闥之長扃。咨遠臣之眇眇兮，感凶諱以怛驚，心孤絕而靡告兮，紛流涕而交頸。思恩榮以橫奔兮，閡闕塞之嶢崢，顧衰絰以輕舉兮，迫關防之我嬰。欲高飛而遙憩兮，憚天網之遠經，遙投骨於山足兮，報恩養於下庭。慨拊心而自悼兮，懼施重而命輕，嗟微驅之是效兮，甘九死而忘生，幾司命之役籍兮，先黃髮而隕零，天蓋高而察卑兮，冀神明之我聽。獨鬱伊而莫愬兮，追顧景而憐形，奏斯文以寫思兮，結翰墨以敷誠。嗚呼哀哉！」

Previously, the Emperor enjoyed literary scholarship, attended to writing and composition, what he personally collated and completed was bequeathed as a hundred volumes. He also employed various classicists to compile the classics and commentaries, by their type joined with one another, altogether over a thousand volumes, titled as the Huánglǎn. <a href="#annotation-46" id="source-46">[46]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
初，帝好文學，以著述為務，自所勒成垂百篇。又使諸儒撰集經傳，隨類相從，凡千餘篇，號曰皇覽。〔一〕

<a href="#source-46" id="annotation-46">[46]</a> Wèi shū states: When the Emperor was previously at the East Palace,  an epidemic greatly rose, at the time people suffered and died.  The Emperor was deeply emotional and sighed, and to Minister Judge Wáng Lǎng, whom he always respected, wrote a letter that said: “Living, there is seven chǐ of body. Dead, there is only one coffin of soil. Only by establishing virtue and raising reputation can there be no decay. After that there is nothing as good as writing books. Epidemics have repeatedly risen, servicemen and people dying and falling. I alone am what man, to be able to preserve this lifespan?” Therefore he considered and compiled what he had written, the Diǎnlùn,  poems, rhapsodies, altogether over a hundred volumes, gathered various classicists within Sùchéng’s gates,  discussing and debating great meanings, consistently without tiring. He always praised Hàn Emperor Wén’s conduct as a lord, lenient and benevolent, mysterious and silent, attending to the desire to influence the people by virtue, having the airs of a worthy sage. At the time of the literary scholars and various classicists, some believed that although Xiào-Wén was worthy, his intelligence and understanding of state systems did not compare to Jiǎ Yì.  The Emperor because of this wrote the Tàizōng Lùn  stating: “In the past Yǒu Miáo did not submit and Chónghuá danced with shield and battle-axe, Wèi Tuó declared himself Emperor and Xiào-Wén succored him with merciful virtue,  the King of Wú did not attend Court, [Xiào-Wén] bestowed him with table and cane to succor his thoughts, and Heaven’s Under depended on this for calm.  Thus he spread the teachings of the Three Clauses,  the influence of contentedness and fraternity, wishing to allow those people who in past times accumulated fatigue, to be able to stride forward and openly discuss without fearful hearts. Something like Jiǎ Yì’s talent and cleverness, planning and preparing state government, is only the talent of a worthy minister, the quality of Guǎn [Zhòng] and Yàn [Yīng].  How could it compare to Xiào-Wén’s capacity as a great man?” During the Third Year, as Sūn Quán would not submit, he again issued Tàizōng Lùn to Heaven’s Under, to clearly show that he had not wanted to go to war. On another day he also casually said: “Looking back, I also have three matters that I cannot seek to imitate from Hàn Emperor Wén: killing Bó Zhāo,  favoring Dèng Tōng,  and having the consort Shèn wear clothes that did not touch the ground and gather up document bags to make curtains.  I believe that Hàn Wén’s frugality was beyond propriety. To the family of his mother’s brother, he should have only cared for them with favor and should not have lent them authority, so that they violated criminal law and also could not but come to harm.” His desire was to maintain the center way, believing that Emperors and Kings in bearing should be like this.

Hú Chōng’s Wú lì  states: The Emperor had a silk book of his composed Diǎnlùn and poems and rhapsodies gifted to Sūn Quán, and also had a paper copy sent to Zhāng Zhāo.

〔一〕　魏書曰：帝初在東宮，疫癘大起，時人彫傷，帝深感歎，與素所敬者大理王朗書曰：「生有七尺之形，死唯一棺之土，唯立德揚名，可以不朽，其次莫如著篇籍。疫癘數起，士人彫落，余獨何人，能全其壽？」故論撰所著典論、詩賦，蓋百餘篇，集諸儒於肅城門內，講論大義，侃侃無倦。常嘉漢文帝之為君，寬仁玄默，務欲以德化民，有賢聖之風。時文學諸儒，或以為孝文雖賢，其於聰明，通達國體，不如賈誼。帝由是著太宗論曰：「昔有苗不賓，重華舞以干戚，尉佗稱帝，孝文撫以恩德，吳王不朝，錫之几杖以撫其意，而天下賴安；乃弘三章之教，愷悌之化，欲使曩時累息之民，得闊步高談，無危懼之心。若賈誼之才敏，籌畫國政，特賢臣之器，管、晏之姿，豈若孝文大人之量哉？」三年之中，以孫權不服，復頒太宗論于天下，明示不願征伐也。他日又從容言曰：「顧我亦有所不取于漢文帝者三：殺薄昭；幸鄧通；慎夫人衣不曳地，集上書囊為帳帷。以為漢文儉而無法，舅后之家，但當養育以恩而不當假借以權，既觸罪法，又不得不害矣。」其欲秉持中道，以為帝王儀表者如此。胡沖吳曆曰：帝以素書所著典論及詩賦餉孫權，又以紙寫一通與張昭。
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Appraisal States: Emperor Wén was naturally endowed with literary elegance, on using brush completed a work, widely learned and strong memory, talents and arts both furnished. <a href="#annotation-47" id="source-47">[47]</a> If only he had added to it an expansive and broad tolerance, strove with fair and impartial sincerity, chased his ambitions while preserving the way, achieved and expanded a virtuous heart, then compared to the worthy rulers of antiquity, how would there be such a distance?
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
評曰：文帝天資文藻，下筆成章，博聞彊識，才蓺兼該；〔一〕若加之曠大之度，勵以公平之誠，邁志存道，克廣德心，則古之賢主，何遠之有哉！

<a href="#source-47" id="annotation-47">[47]</a> (1)	In Diǎnlùn the Emperor’s Self Narration states: In Chūpíng’s Inaugural [190], Dǒng Zhuó killed the Ruler and poisoned the [Dowager] Empress, overthrew and overturned the Ruling House.  At the time the Four Seas were already destitute from the government of Zhōngpíng [184 - 189], and further loathing [Dǒng] Zhuó’s vicious rebellion, family after family worried of chaos, man after man feared themselves in danger. East of the mountains the Governors and Administrators all used the Chūnqiū’s principle of “Wèi men suppressed Zhōuyù at Pú”  to say that man after man all were able to suppress rebels. Thereupon there was a great raising of Righteous Troops, famed heroes and great vigilantes, wealthy houses and powerful clans, whirling and rising like clouds gathering, ten thousand lǐ joining one another. The brigades of Yǎn and Yù [Provinces] battled at Xíngyáng, the armor of Hénèi militarized Mèngjīn. [Dǒng] Zhuó therefore moved the Great Carriage, shifting the capital west to Cháng’ān. And so east of the mountains, the large linked prefectures and states, the middle fortified cities and towns, the small assembled paths and streets, in turn swallowing and exterminating one another. It happened the Huángjīn flourished in Hǎi and Dài,  mountain bandits were violent in Bìng and Jì [Provinces], riding victories to turn and attack, engulfing and going south. Villages and cities spotted smoke and fled, city walls saw dust [of approaching armies] and dispersed, the Hundred Surnames perished and died, exposed bones like weeds. At the time I was aged five years, and my father, because the world was disturbed and in chaos, taught me to learn to shoot. At six years I knew how to shoot, and he also taught me to ride horse. At eight years I was able to ride and shoot. Because at the time there were many dangers, in every campaign I always accompanied. At Jiàn’ān’s beginning [196], my father campaigned south against Jīng Province, reached Yuān, and Zhāng Xiù surrendered. Within ten days he rebelled, and I lost my elder brother the Filial-Incorruptible [Cáo Áng] Zǐxiū, and my elder cousin Ānmín came to harm.  At the time I was aged ten years, and rode horse to escape. The ways of the civil and military, each according to the times are used. I was born at the end of Zhōngpíng [184 – 189], grew up among weapons and soldiers, and therefore from youth enjoyed the bow and horse, and to now I have not declined, chasing game for ten lǐ, galloping and shooting always at a hundred bù, the days many and body strong, my heart never tired of it. Jiàn’ān Tenth Year [205], having just settled Jì Province, the Huìmò sent tribute of excellent bows, Yān and Dài proffered famed horses.  At the time it was the end of spring, Gōumáng directing the season,  mild breeze fanning things, bow dry and hand supple, grass shallow and beasts fat, with my elder cousin Zǐdān  we hunted to Yè’s west, at the end of the day we hand captured deer of nine, pheasants and hares of thirty. Later the army campaigned south and stopped at Qǔlí, Secretariat Writers Director Xún Yù served a mission to present comforts to the army, and after meeting and conversing with me, [Xún] Yù said: “I have heard that you are skilled at shooting with both left and right. This is a truly difficult ability.” I said: “Your Honor has not yet seen launching from neck and unleashing by mouth, bending down to the horse hooves and looking up to the targets.” [Xún] Yù laughed and said: “Really then?” I said: “The [archery] range has a constant track; the targets have designated places. Even if every shot be a hit, it is not utmost mastery. But riding on open plains, racing across dense grasses, pursuing cunning beasts, intercepting light birds, ensuring the bow never be bent in vain, every shot certain to pierce through, then that would be mastery.” At the time Army Libationer Zhāng Jīng  was seated, and looking to [Xún] Yù clapped his hands and said: “Excellent!” I also learned sword fencing, and studied many masters, across the Four Quarters the techniques are each unique, but only the masters of the capital are the best. During the times of Huán and Líng, there was a Tiger Elite Wáng Yuè  who excelled in these techniques, and was praised by the capital masters. Hénán’s Shǐ Ā  said that he in the past traveled with [Wáng] Yuè, completely learned his methods, and I studied under [Shǐ] Ā to learn its essential skills. Once I was with Pacifying Caitiffs General Liú Xūn and Exerting Authority General Dèng Zhǎn and others together drinking.  Previously I had heard that [Dèng] Zhǎn was strong in arm, had learned the Five Weapons,  and also had been praised as being able to use bare hands against naked blades. I discussed swords with him for a good while, and said that the General's skills were not as said, that I had always enjoyed these things, and also had obtained excellent skills, and therefore asked him to face me. At the time we were so intoxicated that our ears burned, and just happened to be eating sugar canes, so we used them as sticks, went down from the Hall and repeatedly sparred, three times striking his arm, and those left and right greatly laughed. [Dèng] Zhǎn was dissatisfied, and requested to go again. I said that my technique was of a fast sort, difficult to use to strike the face, and therefore only struck the arms. [Dèng] Zhǎn said he wished to spar one more time. I knew he wished to charge to seek to engage the center and therefore feigned a deep advance. [Dèng] Zhǎn indeed charged ahead, but I on merely pulling back my leg struck right on his forehead, and those seated and watching were startled. I returned to my seat, and laughed and said: “In the past Yáng Qīng had Chúnyú Yì abandon his former methods, and again receive instruction in secret techniques.  Now I also wish for General Dèng [Zhǎn] to abandon his former tricks, and again receive instruction on the important principles.” All those seated were thoroughly entertained. [But] in such matters, one cannot really call oneself great. When young I learned dual wielding, and myself said that I was without match. Commonly dual halberds are called ‘sitting in iron chamber,’ side shields are called ‘the covering wooden door.’ Later I studied under Chén state’s Yuán Mǐn,  who used one [weapon] to fight dual [wielding], in every match he was like a spirit, the opponent did not know where he would strike out. In those former days if I had encountered [Yuán] Mǐn on a narrow road, [the duel] would have at once be decided [against me]! With other games I had few that I enjoyed, only in playing Dànqí  was I somewhat thorough in the skill, and when young made a rhapsody for it. In the past in the capital the foremost players were Mǎ the Marquess of Hé village, Dōngfāng Ānshì, and young noble Zhāng,  and I always regret that I could not have played against these masters. My father greatly enjoyed the Shī [jīng] and [Shàng] Shū and literature. Although he was in the army, his hands did not set aside books, and always studied them when at ease, always saying: “Men who are studious when young are able to think hard, but when grown are forgetful. Those grown up but still able to be diligent in study are only me and Yuán Bóyè.”  I therefore when young recited [from memory] the Shī [jīng] and Lún [yǔ], and when grown studied through the words of the Five Classics, the Four Genres, the Shǐ[jì] and Hàn[shū], and the Hundred Schools of thought,  and there was none I did not read.

Bówùzhì states: The Emperor was skilled in Dànqí, able to use a hand towel’s corner. At the time there was a scholar, also able to lower his head to use his cap’s hemp headscarf corner to cast the pieces.

〔一〕　典論帝自敘曰：初平之元，董卓殺主鴆后，蕩覆王室。是時四海既困中平之政，兼惡卓之凶逆，家家思亂，人人自危。山東牧守，咸以春秋之義，「衛人討州吁于濮」，言人人皆得討賊。於是大興義兵，名豪大俠，富室強族，飄揚雲會，萬里相赴；兗、豫之師戰于滎陽，河內之甲軍于孟津。卓遂遷大駕，西都長安。而山東大者連郡國，中者嬰城邑，小者聚阡陌，以還相吞滅。會黃巾盛於海、岱，山寇暴於并、冀，乘勝轉攻，席卷而南，鄉邑望煙而奔，城郭睹塵而潰，百姓死亡，暴骨如莽。余時年五歲，上以世方擾亂，教余學射，六歲而知射，又教余騎馬，八歲而能騎射矣。以時之多故，每征，余常從。建安初，上南征荊州，至宛，張繡降。旬日而反，亡兄孝廉子修、從兄安民遇害。時余年十歲，乘馬得脫。夫文武之道，各隨時而用，生于中平之季，長于戎旅之間，是以少好弓馬，于今不衰；逐禽輒十里，馳射常百步，日多體健，心每不厭。建安十年，始定冀州，濊、貊貢良弓，燕、代獻名馬。時歲之暮春，勾芒司節，和風扇物，弓燥手柔，草淺獸肥，與族兄子丹獵于鄴西，終日手獲獐鹿九，雉兔三十。後軍南征次曲蠡，尚書令荀彧奉使犒軍，見余談論之末，彧言：「聞君善左右射，此實難能。」余言：「執事未睹夫項發口縱，俯馬蹄而仰月支也。」彧喜笑曰：「乃爾！」余曰：「埒有常徑，的有常所，雖每發輒中，非至妙也。若馳平原，赴豐草，要狡獸，截輕禽，使弓不虛彎，所中必洞，斯則妙矣。」時軍祭酒張京在坐，顧彧拊手曰「善」。余又學擊劍，閱師多矣，四方之法各異，唯京師為善。桓、靈之間，有虎賁王越善斯術，稱於京師。河南史阿言昔與越遊，具得其法，余從阿學之精熟。嘗與平虜將軍劉勳、奮威將軍鄧展等共飲，宿聞展善有手臂，曉五兵，又稱其能空手入白刃。余與論劍良久，謂言將軍法非也，余顧嘗好之，又得善術，因求與余對。時酒酣耳熱，方食芊蔗，便以為杖，下殿數交，三中其臂，左右大笑。展意不平，求更為之。余言吾法急屬，難相中面，故齊臂耳。展言願復一交，余知其欲突以取交中也，因偽深進，展果尋前，余卻腳鄛，正截其顙，坐中驚視。余還坐，笑曰：「昔陽慶使淳于意去其故方，更授以祕術，今余亦願鄧將軍捐棄故伎，更受要道也。」一坐盡歡。夫事不可自謂己長，余少曉持複，自謂無對；俗名雙戟為坐鐵室，鑲楯為蔽木戶；後從陳國袁敏學，以單攻複，每為若神，對家不知所出，先日若逢敏於狹路，直決耳！余於他戲弄之事少所喜，唯彈棋略盡其巧，少為之賦。昔京師先工有馬合鄉侯、東方安世、張公子，常恨不得與彼數子者對。上雅好詩書文籍，雖在軍旅，手不釋卷，每每定省從容，常言人少好學則思專，長則善忘，長大而能勤學者，唯吾與袁伯業耳。余是以少誦詩、論，及長而備歷五經、四部，史、漢、諸子百家之言，靡不畢覽。博物志曰：帝善彈棋，能用手巾角。時有一書生，又能低頭以所冠著葛巾角撇棋。
